events.description: On December 17, 1992, the leaders of Mexico, Canada, and the United States signed the North American Free Trade Agreement. It was replaced by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement in 2020.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 17

events.title: Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premieres
events.summary: The ballet is first performed at the Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg.
events.description: On December 18, 1892, Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker was first presented at the Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg, Russia.
events.notificationBody: In 1892, Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premiered in St. Petersburg.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

images.altText: Photograph of Stanislava Belinskaya as Clara in the original 1892 production of The Nutcracker
images.creator: Unknown photographer, Imperial Mariinsky Theatre
images.attribution: Unknown photographer, Imperial Mariinsky Theatre, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: The Thirteenth Amendment abolishes slavery in the US
events.summary: The constitutional amendment officially enters into force.
events.description: On December 18, 1865, the Thirteenth Amendment to the US Constitution officially entered into force, abolishing slavery in the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: The Piltdown Man is announced
events.summary: A supposed 'missing link' fossil later proves to be a fraud.
events.description: On December 18, 1912, a British Museum paleontologist announced the discovery in England of fossil remains said to be an extinct human species. Presented as a missing link between apes and early humans, the Piltdown Man was exposed as a fraud by the 1950s.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: Antonio Stradivari dies in Cremona
events.summary: The famed Italian violin maker dies.
events.description: On December 18, 1737, the famed Italian violin maker Antonio Stradivari died in Cremona.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: Charles Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol
events.summary: Scrooge's story of redemption becomes an instant classic.
events.description: On December 19, 1843, Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol was published for the first time. Its story of Ebenezer Scrooge's redemption became an instant classic and is still retold on stage and screen.
events.notificationTitle: Bah, humbug, and a classic is born
events.notificationBody: In 1843, Charles Dickens published A Christmas Carol.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

images.altText: John Leech's colour frontispiece of Mr Fezziwig's Ball from the first edition of A Christmas Carol
images.creator: John Leech
images.attribution: John Leech, via Wikimedia Commons (CC0 1.0)

events.title: Washington's army goes into winter quarters at Valley Forge
events.summary: About 11,000 Continental troops camp near British-occupied Philadelphia.
events.description: On December 19, 1777, during the American Revolution, General George Washington led 11,000 regulars into winter quarters at Valley Forge, on the Schuylkill River near British-occupied Philadelphia.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: Edith Piaf is born in Paris
events.summary: The singer who made the French chanson world famous is born.
events.description: On December 19, 1915, the singer and actress Edith Piaf, whose interpretation of the French chanson made her internationally famous, was born in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: South Korea elects its first woman president
events.summary: Park Geun-hye wins the presidential election.
events.description: On December 19, 2012, Park Geun-hye was elected the first female president of South Korea. She later became the country's first democratically elected president to be removed from office, after her impeachment in 2017.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: The Brothers Grimm publish their first volume of tales
events.summary: Stories like Hansel and Gretel and Snow White reach print.
events.description: On December 20, 1812, the brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm published the first volume of the stories that made them famous. Their collection, known as Grimm's Fairy Tales, includes 'Hansel and Gretel', 'Snow White', 'Little Red Riding Hood', and 'Sleeping Beauty'.
events.notificationTitle: Once upon a time, in print
events.notificationBody: In 1812, the Brothers Grimm published their first volume of fairy tales.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

images.altText: 1855 double portrait of the brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm
images.creator: Elisabeth Baumann
images.attribution: Elisabeth Baumann, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Macau returns to Chinese sovereignty
events.summary: Centuries of Portuguese rule come to an end.
events.description: On December 20, 1999, centuries of Portuguese rule in Macau ended when it became a special administrative region under Chinese sovereignty, 12 years after China and Portugal agreed on its status.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: It's a Wonderful Life premieres
events.summary: Frank Capra's drama becomes a holiday classic.
events.description: On December 20, 1946, Frank Capra's It's a Wonderful Life, starring Jimmy Stewart, premiered. It later became a holiday classic.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: South Carolina secedes from the Union
events.summary: The first state to leave follows Lincoln's election.
events.description: On December 20, 1860, following Abraham Lincoln's election as president, South Carolina became the first US state to secede from the Union.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: The first game of basketball is played
events.summary: James Naismith's new game debuts in a Springfield school gym.
events.description: On December 21, 1891, the first game of basketball, organized by gym teacher James Naismith, was played at a school in Springfield, Massachusetts. The chaotic game prompted Naismith to develop the sport's original rules.
events.notificationBody: In 1891, the first game of basketball was played in Springfield.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

images.altText: James Naismith, inventor of basketball, holding a ball and a peach basket
images.creator: Unknown author
images.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Apollo 8 launches toward the Moon
events.summary: The mission will complete ten lunar orbits.
events.description: On December 21, 1968, Apollo 8 was launched from Cape Kennedy and went on to complete 10 orbits of the Moon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: The first modern crossword puzzle is published
events.summary: The New York World introduces a new kind of word game.
events.description: On December 21, 1913, the New York World published the first modern crossword puzzle.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: The Brandenburg Gate reopens
events.summary: Berliners pass through the gate for the first time since 1961.
events.description: On December 22, 1989, the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin reopened as East and West Germany moved toward reunification. Berliners had been unable to use the gate since the Berlin Wall blocked it in 1961.
events.notificationBody: In 1989, Berlin's Brandenburg Gate reopened after 28 years.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

images.altText: German politicians at the official opening of the Brandenburg Gate crossing on December 22, 1989
images.creator: SSgt. F. Lee Corkran
images.attribution: SSgt. F. Lee Corkran, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Srinivasa Ramanujan is born
events.summary: The self-taught Indian mathematician is born in Erode.
events.description: On December 22, 1887, Srinivasa Ramanujan, a self-taught Indian mathematician who made many pioneering discoveries, was born in Erode in present-day Tamil Nadu.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: The pope sanctions the Dominican order
events.summary: Honorius III approves the Order of Preachers.
events.description: On December 22, 1216, the Dominican order was sanctioned by Pope Honorius III.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: Leo the Deacon records the solar corona during an eclipse
events.summary: Leo the Deacon's account is the earliest datable description of the corona.
events.description: On December 22, 968, an eclipse of the Sun occurred, and Leo the Deacon described a feeble glow, like a narrow headband, around the darkened Sun: the earliest account of the solar corona that can be linked to a datable eclipse.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: George Washington resigns as commander in chief
events.summary: The victorious general returns his commission to Congress.
events.description: On December 23, 1783, before the Continental Congress, George Washington resigned as commander in chief of the Continental Army.
events.notificationTitle: The general who gave back his power
events.notificationBody: In 1783, George Washington resigned as commander in chief.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

images.altText: John Trumbull painting of George Washington resigning his commission before Congress in 1783
images.creator: John Trumbull
images.attribution: John Trumbull, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: The Ottoman Empire's first constitution takes effect
events.summary: The document gives the sultan full executive power.
events.description: On December 23, 1876, the first comprehensive constitution of the Ottoman Empire went into effect, giving the sultan full executive power.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: The Federal Reserve System is created
events.summary: President Wilson signs the Federal Reserve Act.
events.description: On December 23, 1913, President Woodrow Wilson signed the Federal Reserve Act, bringing the Federal Reserve System into being.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: Jean-Francois Champollion is born
events.summary: The French linguist and historian is born.
events.description: On December 23, 1790, the French historian and linguist Jean-Francois Champollion was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: Edison applies to patent the phonograph
events.summary: The 'speaking machine' is filed with the US Patent Office.
events.description: On December 24, 1877, the US Patent Office received Thomas Edison's application for a 'Phonograph or Speaking Machine'. He had first demonstrated the device weeks earlier by playing back his recorded voice.
events.notificationBody: In 1877, Thomas Edison applied to patent the phonograph.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

images.altText: Thomas Edison's 1877 tinfoil cylinder phonograph with its hand crank
images.creator: National Park Service
images.attribution: National Park Service, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: The Treaty of Ghent ends the War of 1812
events.summary: The United States and Britain make peace in Belgium.
events.description: On December 24, 1814, the United States and Great Britain signed the Treaty of Ghent in Belgium, ending the War of 1812.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: Libya becomes independent under King Idris I
events.summary: The new North African kingdom crowns its first monarch.
events.description: On December 24, 1951, Idris I became the first king of newly independent Libya.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: The James Webb Space Telescope launches
events.summary: Hubble's successor lifts off on Christmas Day.
events.description: On December 25, 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope, designed and built by US, Canadian, and European space agencies as the successor to the Hubble Space Telescope, was launched into space.
events.notificationBody: On Christmas Day 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope launched.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
events.summary: The king of the Franks becomes the first emperor of the Holy Roman Empire.
events.description: On December 25, 800, Charlemagne, king of the Franks, became the first emperor of what became the Holy Roman Empire.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: William the Conqueror is crowned king of England
events.summary: The coronation completes the Norman Conquest.
events.description: On December 25, 1066, William I was crowned king of England, formally completing the Norman Conquest.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Washington crosses the Delaware
events.summary: A Christmas night crossing leads to a surprise attack at Trenton.
events.description: On December 25, 1776, during the American Revolution, General George Washington crossed the Delaware River and surprised the British at Trenton, New Jersey.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president
events.summary: The Soviet Union ceases to exist at the end of the year.
events.description: On December 25, 1991, Mikhail Gorbachev resigned the presidency of the Soviet Union, which ceased to exist at the end of the year.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Eleven countries adopt the euro
events.summary: Europe's single currency is launched.
events.description: On January 1, 1999, eleven European Union countries adopted the euro as their currency.
events.notificationBody: In 1999, eleven European countries adopted the euro.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

images.altText: A row of euro coins of different values
images.creator: Vander
images.attribution: Vander, via Wikimedia Commons (CC0 1.0)

events.title: Haiti declares independence from France
events.summary: The Haitian Revolution ends with a new independent nation.
events.description: On January 1, 1804, Haiti declared its independence from France, bringing the Haitian Revolution to an end.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

events.title: Lincoln issues the Emancipation Proclamation
events.summary: The order frees enslaved people in the Confederacy.
events.description: On January 1, 1863, US President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation, which freed enslaved people in the Confederacy.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

events.title: The World Trade Organization is established
events.summary: A new global body oversees international trade rules.
events.description: On January 1, 1995, the World Trade Organization was formally established.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

events.title: Fulgencio Batista flees Cuba
events.summary: Fidel Castro's rebels topple the dictator's regime.
events.description: On January 1, 1959, the dictator Fulgencio Batista fled Cuba after his regime was toppled by rebel forces led by Fidel Castro.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 1

events.title: Wham-O is granted a patent for the Frisbee
events.summary: A US patent covers 'a saucer-shaped throwing implement'.
events.description: On December 26, 1967, the Wham-O Manufacturing Company was issued a US patent for what it called a saucer-shaped throwing implement, better known as the Frisbee.
events.notificationBody: In 1967, Wham-O was granted a patent for its flying disc, the Frisbee.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

images.altText: A red Wham-O Frisbee flying disc from 1966
images.creator: UnifiedFunctionality
images.attribution: UnifiedFunctionality, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

events.title: Mao Zedong is born
events.summary: The future first chairman of the People's Republic of China is born.
events.description: On December 26, 1893, Mao Zedong was born. A Marxist theorist and revolutionary, he became the first chairman of the People's Republic of China, serving from 1949 to 1959.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: An earthquake off Sumatra triggers the Indian Ocean tsunami
events.summary: A massive undersea earthquake sends a devastating tsunami across the Indian Ocean.
events.description: On December 26, 2004, a massive earthquake shook the Indian Ocean floor west of the island of Sumatra, triggering a devastating tsunami that struck coastlines across the region.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: Charles Babbage is born in London
events.summary: The mathematician and inventor of early calculating machines is born.
events.description: On December 26, 1791, the mathematician and inventor Charles Babbage, a pioneer of mechanical computing, was born in London.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: Jack Johnson wins the world heavyweight title
events.summary: He becomes the first Black world heavyweight boxing champion.
events.description: On December 26, 1908, Jack Johnson defeated Tommy Burns in Sydney, Australia, to become the first Black fighter to win the world heavyweight boxing championship.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 26

events.title: Hagia Sophia is consecrated in Constantinople
events.summary: The great domed church becomes the largest in the world.
events.description: On December 27, 537, the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople was consecrated as a church. It was then the largest church in the world.
events.notificationTitle: A dome that awed an empire
events.notificationBody: In 537, the Hagia Sophia was consecrated in Constantinople.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

images.altText: Hagia Sophia in Istanbul, with its great central dome and four minarets
images.creator: Arild Vågen
images.attribution: Arild Vågen, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

events.title: Charles Darwin sets sail on HMS Beagle
events.summary: The voyage will shape his theory of evolution.
events.description: On December 27, 1831, Charles Darwin set sail on HMS Beagle, beginning the voyage during which he would formulate his theory of evolution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: Johannes Kepler is born
events.summary: The astronomer will discover three laws of planetary motion.
events.description: On December 27, 1571, the German astronomer Johannes Kepler was born. He discovered three major laws of planetary motion.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: The Netherlands transfers sovereignty to Indonesia
events.summary: Dutch control ends four years after Indonesia declared independence.
events.description: On December 27, 1949, the Dutch formally relinquished control over Indonesia, which had declared its independence in 1945.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: Benazir Bhutto is assassinated
events.summary: Pakistan's former prime minister is killed while campaigning.
events.description: On December 27, 2007, Benazir Bhutto, former prime minister of Pakistan, was assassinated in Rawalpindi while campaigning in parliamentary elections.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 27

events.title: The Lumiere brothers' Cinematographe makes its public debut
events.summary: Moving pictures are shown to the public at the Grand Cafe in Paris.
events.description: On December 28, 1895, the first public demonstration of the Lumiere brothers' Cinematographe took place at the Grand Cafe in Paris, a landmark in the birth of cinema.
events.notificationTitle: The first night at the movies
events.notificationBody: In 1895, the Lumiere brothers screened films to the public in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 28

images.altText: Portrait photograph of the brothers Auguste and Louis Lumiere, around 1895
images.creator: Unknown author
images.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Edward the Confessor's church at Westminster is consecrated
events.summary: The king's new abbey church is consecrated, though he is too ill to attend.
events.description: On December 28, 1065, the new abbey church that Edward the Confessor had built at Westminster was consecrated. The king was too ill to attend the service and died about a week later.

sources.name: Westminster Abbey - Edward the Confessor and Edith

events.title: The Indian National Congress meets for the first time
events.summary: The party that will lead India's independence movement holds its first session.
events.description: On December 28, 1885, the first session of the Indian National Congress convened. The party later led the movement for India's independence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 28

events.title: The US Endangered Species Act is signed
events.summary: Richard Nixon signs a landmark wildlife protection law.
events.description: On December 28, 1973, US President Richard Nixon signed the Endangered Species Act into law.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 28

events.title: The Irish Free State becomes Ireland
events.summary: A new constitution renames the state.
events.description: On December 29, 1937, with the enactment of a new constitution, the Irish Free State became known as Ireland.
events.notificationTitle: A new name for a nation
events.notificationBody: In 1937, a new constitution turned the Irish Free State into Ireland.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

images.altText: Irish postage stamp issued on December 29, 1937, to mark the new Constitution of Ireland
images.creator: Richard J. King for the Department of Posts and Telegraphs
images.attribution: Richard J. King for the Department of Posts and Telegraphs, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Texas joins the Union as a state
events.summary: The former Republic of Texas is admitted to the United States.
events.description: On December 29, 1845, Texas, until then an independent republic, legally entered the Union as a US state when Congress accepted its state constitution. Congress had passed the annexation resolution on February 28, 1845.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29
Texas State Historical Association - Handbook of Texas: Annexation

events.title: William Gladstone is born in Liverpool
events.summary: The future four-time British prime minister is born.
events.description: On December 29, 1809, William Ewart Gladstone was born in Liverpool. He served as prime minister of Great Britain four times between 1868 and 1894.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

events.title: The Wounded Knee Massacre
events.summary: US troops kill Lakota people at Wounded Knee Creek in South Dakota.
events.description: On December 29, 1890, US Army troops carried out the Wounded Knee Massacre in South Dakota. It was the last major armed conflict between the United States and the Plains peoples.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

events.title: Guinea is declared free of Ebola
events.summary: The WHO declares the end of transmission two years after the outbreak began.
events.description: On December 29, 2015, the World Health Organization declared Guinea free of Ebola, some two years after the deadly disease was reported in the country.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 29

events.title: The Soviet Union is established
events.summary: The USSR is founded with its capital in Moscow.
events.description: On December 30, 1922, the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was established, with its capital in Moscow.
events.notificationBody: In 1922, the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was established.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

images.altText: First page of the 1922 Declaration and Treaty on the Creation of the USSR
images.creator: Government of the Soviet Union
images.attribution: Government of the Soviet Union, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Jose Rizal is executed in Manila
events.summary: The Philippine national hero is put to death by Spanish authorities.
events.description: On December 30, 1896, Jose Rizal, the writer and reformer regarded as a national hero of the Philippines, was publicly executed by the country's Spanish rulers.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: The Gadsden Purchase is signed
events.summary: The United States buys nearly 30,000 square miles from Mexico.
events.description: On December 30, 1853, the United States acquired nearly 30,000 square miles of northern Mexican territory with the signing of the Gadsden Purchase.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: Robert Falcon Scott sets a farthest-south record
events.summary: His party pushes deeper into Antarctica than anyone before.
events.description: On December 30, 1902, the British explorer Robert Falcon Scott set a new record for reaching the farthest point south, on the Ross Ice Shelf.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: The Treaty of Surji-Arjungaon is signed
events.summary: A Maratha chief cedes territory and power in India to the British.
events.description: On December 30, 1803, the Maratha chief Daulat Rao Sindhia signed the Treaty of Surji-Arjungaon, ceding political power and territory in India to the British.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 30

events.title: The first ball drops in Times Square
events.summary: New York City starts a New Year's Eve tradition.
events.description: On December 31, 1907, the first ball was dropped at Times Square in New York City to celebrate New Year's Eve, beginning a tradition that continues today.
events.notificationBody: In 1907, the first New Year's Eve ball dropped in Times Square.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: The English East India Company is chartered
events.summary: A royal charter launches the company for trade with Asia.
events.description: On December 31, 1600, the East India Company, formed to exploit trade with East and Southeast Asia and India, was incorporated by English royal charter.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: Queen Victoria names Ottawa the capital of Canada
events.summary: The city is chosen as the national capital.
events.description: On December 31, 1857, Queen Victoria named Ottawa the national capital of Canada.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: The United States hands the Panama Canal to Panama
events.summary: Panama takes full control of the canal.
events.description: On December 31, 1999, the United States officially handed over control of the Panama Canal to Panama.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: Taipei 101 opens as the world's tallest building
events.summary: The 508-metre tower opens in Taiwan's capital.
events.description: On December 31, 2004, Taipei 101 opened in Taipei, Taiwan. At 1,667 feet (508 metres), it was then the tallest building in the world.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 31

events.title: Ferdinand and Isabella capture Granada
events.summary: The fall of the last Muslim kingdom in Spain ends centuries of campaigns.
events.description: On January 2, 1492, Ferdinand II and Isabella I, the first monarchs of a unified Spain, captured Granada, ending a centuries-long series of military campaigns on the Iberian Peninsula.
events.notificationTitle: The end of an era in Spain
events.notificationBody: In 1492, Ferdinand and Isabella captured Granada.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 2

images.altText: Francisco Pradilla painting of Muhammad XII surrendering Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella
images.creator: Francisco Pradilla y Ortiz
images.attribution: Francisco Pradilla y Ortiz, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Russia surrenders Port Arthur to Japan
events.summary: A major Russian defeat in the Russo-Japanese War.
events.description: On January 2, 1905, during the Russo-Japanese War, Russian forces surrendered Port Arthur (later Lushun, China) to the Japanese.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 2

events.title: NASA's Stardust collects dust from a comet
events.summary: The spacecraft gathers grains from comet Wild 2.
events.description: On January 2, 2004, NASA's Stardust spacecraft collected dust grains from the comet Wild 2.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 2

events.title: The Palmer Raids sweep US cities
events.summary: Thousands are arrested as suspected radicals.
events.description: On January 2, 1920, in the Palmer Raids, thousands of people were arrested in more than 30 US cities, accused of being foreign anarchists, communists, or radical leftists.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 2

events.title: J.R.R. Tolkien is born
events.summary: The author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings is born.
events.description: On January 3, 1892, J.R.R. Tolkien, author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, was born in Bloemfontein, South Africa.
events.notificationBody: In 1892, J.R.R. Tolkien, author of The Lord of the Rings, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3
Encyclopaedia Britannica - J.R.R. Tolkien

events.title: Alaska becomes the 49th US state
events.summary: The former territory joins the Union.
events.description: On January 3, 1959, Alaska became the 49th state of the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: China's Chang'e 4 lands on the far side of the Moon
events.summary: It is the first spacecraft to land on the lunar far side.
events.description: On January 3, 2019, China's Chang'e 4 spacecraft, carrying the Yutu-2 rover, landed on the far side of the Moon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: Pope Leo X excommunicates Martin Luther
events.summary: The break between Luther and Rome becomes formal.
events.description: On January 3, 1521, Pope Leo X excommunicated Martin Luther.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: Washington wins the Battle of Princeton
events.summary: American forces win a battle in New Jersey.
events.description: On January 3, 1777, during the American Revolution, the Battle of Princeton was fought in New Jersey.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: Louis Braille is born
events.summary: The inventor of the raised-dot writing system is born near Paris.
events.description: On January 4, 1809, Louis Braille, who developed the system of printing and writing for the blind that bears his name, was born near Paris.
events.notificationBody: In 1809, Louis Braille, inventor of the braille system, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

images.altText: Engraved portrait of Louis Braille
images.creator: Henri Thiriat
images.attribution: Henri Thiriat, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Burma gains independence from Britain
events.summary: The country now called Myanmar becomes independent.
events.description: On January 4, 1948, Burma, today called Myanmar, formally gained independence from Great Britain.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: The Burj Khalifa opens in Dubai
events.summary: The world's tallest building officially opens.
events.description: On January 4, 2010, the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, officially opened in Dubai.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: Albert Camus dies in a car accident
events.summary: The novelist and playwright is killed in France.
events.description: On January 4, 1960, the novelist and playwright Albert Camus was killed in an automobile accident in France.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: Solomon Northup regains his freedom
events.summary: A free Black man kidnapped into slavery is legally freed.
events.description: On January 4, 1853, Solomon Northup, a free Black man who had been kidnapped in Washington, D.C., and sold into slavery, legally obtained his freedom.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: Waiting for Godot is staged for the first time
events.summary: Samuel Beckett's play premieres in Paris.
events.description: On January 5, 1953, Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot was staged for the first time, in Paris.
events.notificationBody: In 1953, Beckett's Waiting for Godot premiered in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: Construction begins on the Golden Gate Bridge
events.summary: Work starts on the bridge linking San Francisco and Marin county.
events.description: On January 5, 1933, construction began on the Golden Gate Bridge, which connects San Francisco with Marin county.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: The dwarf planet Eris is discovered
events.summary: Astronomers spot it in images taken in 2003.
events.description: On January 5, 2005, the dwarf planet Eris was discovered in images taken in 2003 at Palomar Observatory.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: Nellie Tayloe Ross becomes the first woman US governor
events.summary: She takes office in Wyoming.
events.description: On January 5, 1925, Nellie Tayloe Ross took office in Wyoming, becoming the first woman governor in the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt outlines the Four Freedoms
events.summary: His State of the Union message names four essential freedoms.
events.description: On January 6, 1941, US President Franklin D. Roosevelt outlined his Four Freedoms in his State of the Union message.
events.notificationBody: In 1941, Franklin D. Roosevelt set out his Four Freedoms.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Henry VIII marries Anne of Cleves
events.summary: She becomes the fourth of his six wives.
events.description: On January 6, 1540, Henry VIII of England married Anne of Cleves, the fourth of his six wives.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Britain recognizes the People's Republic of China
events.summary: The UK formally recognizes the new Communist government.
events.description: On January 6, 1950, Great Britain announced its recognition of the People's Republic of China.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Composer Max Bruch is born
events.summary: The Romantic composer is born in Cologne.
events.description: On January 6, 1838, the composer Max Bruch was born in Cologne, in what is today Germany.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Richard II of England is born
events.summary: The future king will reign from 1377 to 1399.
events.description: On January 6, 1367, the future King Richard II of England was born. He reigned from 1377 to 1399.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Marian Anderson sings at the Metropolitan Opera
events.summary: The contralto performs with the Met for the first time.
events.description: On January 7, 1955, the American contralto Marian Anderson first performed with the Metropolitan Opera in New York City, becoming the first Black singer to perform as a member of the company. She sang Ulrica in Verdi's Un ballo in maschera.
events.notificationTitle: A voice that opened the Met
events.notificationBody: In 1955, Marian Anderson made her Metropolitan Opera debut.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Marian Anderson

events.title: Vietnamese forces take Phnom Penh
events.summary: The Khmer Rouge regime of Pol Pot is driven from power.
events.description: On January 7, 1979, Vietnamese forces took control of Phnom Penh, Cambodia, removing the Khmer Rouge and Pol Pot from power.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: Surveyor 7 launches toward the Moon
events.summary: The uncrewed probe will make a soft lunar landing.
events.description: On January 7, 1968, the uncrewed US space probe Surveyor 7 was launched; it went on to make a soft landing on the Moon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: Egypt marks Christmas as a national holiday
events.summary: Coptic Christmas becomes a public holiday for the first time.
events.description: On January 7, 2003, Christmas was celebrated as a national holiday in Egypt for the first time.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: John Kufuor is inaugurated in Ghana
events.summary: Ghana completes its first peaceful transfer of power between governments.
events.description: On January 7, 2001, John Kufuor was inaugurated as president of Ghana in the country's first peaceful transition of government.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: The African National Congress is founded
events.summary: The movement that will lead the struggle against apartheid is born.
events.description: On January 8, 1912, the African National Congress was founded in South Africa.
events.notificationBody: In 1912, the African National Congress was founded in South Africa.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

images.altText: The South African Native National Congress delegation to England in 1914, two years after the party's founding

images.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

events.title: Woodrow Wilson announces his Fourteen Points
events.summary: The US president sets out his plan for peace after World War I.
events.description: On January 8, 1918, US President Woodrow Wilson announced his Fourteen Points, a program for peace after World War I.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

events.title: Charles de Gaulle becomes president of the Fifth Republic
events.summary: France's new constitutional order gets its first president.
events.description: On January 8, 1959, Charles de Gaulle was inaugurated as president of France's Fifth Republic.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

events.title: Stephen Hawking is born
events.summary: The physicist known for his work on black holes is born.
events.description: On January 8, 1942, the physicist Stephen Hawking was born. He developed a theory of exploding black holes.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

events.title: Elvis Presley is born
events.summary: The future 'King of Rock and Roll' is born.
events.description: On January 8, 1935, Elvis Presley, widely known as the King of Rock and Roll, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

events.title: The trial of Joan of Arc begins
events.summary: The 19-year-old faces more than 70 accusations.
events.description: On January 9, 1431, Joan of Arc, then 19 years old, was put on trial in Rouen, France, facing more than 70 accusations. Two years earlier she had led the French to victory at Orleans.
events.notificationTitle: Joan of Arc goes on trial
events.notificationBody: In 1431, the trial of Joan of Arc began in Rouen.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 9
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Saint Joan of Arc

events.title: Simone de Beauvoir is born in Paris
events.summary: The writer and feminist thinker is born.
events.description: On January 9, 1908, Simone de Beauvoir, a writer and feminist who gave literary form to the themes of existentialism, was born in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 9

events.title: Mahmoud Abbas is elected Palestinian Authority president
events.summary: He succeeds Yasser Arafat as leader of the Palestinian Authority.
events.description: On January 9, 2005, Mahmoud Abbas was elected president of the Palestinian Authority.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 9

events.title: Apple introduces iTunes
events.summary: The digital media player changes how people buy and play music.
events.description: On January 9, 2001, Apple introduced iTunes, a digital media player application that went on to revolutionize digital music.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 9

events.title: Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon
events.dateNote: Traditional date in the pre-Julian Roman calendar.
events.summary: Caesar leads his army into Italy, starting a civil war.
events.description: On January 10, 49 BCE, Julius Caesar and his army crossed the Rubicon to take control of the Roman Republic, a step that began a civil war.
events.notificationBody: In 49 BCE, Julius Caesar led his army across the Rubicon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 10

events.title: Thomas Paine publishes Common Sense
events.summary: The pamphlet calls for American independence.
events.description: On January 10, 1776, Thomas Paine published Common Sense, a 50-page pamphlet that sold more than 500,000 copies within a few months and called for a war of independence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 10

events.title: The League of Nations is established
events.summary: The first international peacekeeping organization comes into being.
events.description: On January 10, 1920, the League of Nations was established, with its headquarters in Geneva.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 10

events.title: The first UN General Assembly meets in London
events.summary: Delegates of the new United Nations gather for the first time.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 11

events.summary: The future prime minister of Canada is born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 11

events.title: Berry Gordy launches Tamla Records

events.title: Britain ends the state of emergency in Kenya

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 12

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 13

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 13

events.title: The Costa Concordia runs aground off Italy

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 13

events.title: The Huygens probe lands on Titan

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 14

events.title: Congress ratifies the Treaty of Paris
events.summary: The peace formally ends the American Revolution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 14

events.title: The British Museum opens to the public

events.title: Wikipedia launches

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 15

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 15

events.dateNote: New Style date; January 6 in the Old Style calendar then used in Britain's colonies.

The plutonium bomb, built under William Penney after a 1947 government decision to make a British atomic bomb, had an estimated yield of 25 kilotons. By early 1954 RAF Canberra bombers were armed with atomic bombs.
